item.title: First Thing: Cop31 talks collapse without deal in blow to planet’s future climate
item.description:
More than two weeks of talks in Turkey fail to produce a resolution to tackle climate crisis. Plus, a savage review of Melania’s new documentary Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Good morning. The world’s nations have failed to reach agreement at the Cop31 talks in Turkey. In a dramatic conclusion to the summit, major powers rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels. The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien. What was in the proposed agreement? The Antalya pact invited nations to electrify their economies, called on wealthy countries to fund climate adaptation for poorer ones, and urged signatories to minimise any “overshoot” of the Paris agreement’s 1.5C global heating threshold. item.title: 'Out of control': ICE agents make arrests at Seattle airport in 'horrific' scene
item.description:

ICE officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month's midterms.

item.title: US army to blow up bomb-making chemicals despite safety concerns
item.description:
The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is in Middletown, Iowa, a small town is about 8 miles west of Burlington in southeast, Iowa. Scott Olson/Getty Images The U.S. Army set off waves of anxiety in Iowa in mid-November when it confirmed plans to carry out two controlled explosions at an ammunition plant, explosions that are expected to send a plume of lead particles – a neurotoxin – over homes and farmland for miles. Late on Nov. 22, 2026, the Army announced the rescheduled date: Nov. 25 , the day before Thanksgiving. According to the Army, dozens of old barrels containing lead azide , an explosive used as a detonator, have become unstable and pose an “ unacceptable risk of accidental detonation ” at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. item.title: UN’s COP31 Climate Conference Fizzles Out as Global Policy Divides Deepen
item.description:
On the day the largest global climate summit started earlier this month, my colleague Rachel Santarsiero posed a key question : “Will anyone finally say ‘fossil fuels’?” The past three decades of discussions have largely sidestepped the issue despite the fact that fossil fuels are the largest contributor to climate change—and the past two weeks in Turkey have proved no different. Deliberations at COP31, the 31st annual United Nations climate action convention, broke down Sunday after the European Union and other nations rejected the draft agreement setting out commitments to address climate change. “These decisions go nowhere near the level of ambition needed to tackle climate change,” Irish minister Darragh O’Brien, representing the EU at the convention, said Sunday. “It is unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no mention of fossil fuels.” The Panamanian…

item.description:

item.title: Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide
item.description:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn? As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory. Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. item.title: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
item.description:
Students wait for the start of the annual college entrance exams at an exam hall in Seoul on Nov. 19, 2026. —Kim Hong-Ji—Pool/AFP/Getty Images South Korea’s education minister has resigned after intense backlash against new rules meant to prevent cheating using artificial intelligence during the country’s high-stakes college entrance exams. Choi Kyo-jin announced his resignation on Sunday in response to “criticism or blame from the public for failing to prepare adequately in advance.” The Ministry of Education had announced the new exam measures on Tuesday, just two days before nearly 500,000 South Koreans took the hourslong College Scholastic Ability Test, also called Suneung . item.title: Gaza turned into ‘toxic wasteland’ by Israel’s war, says new report
item.description:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’ Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report. Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.
